log was not pulled.Tasks: Existing HubSpot tasks are not surfaced, creating a risk of duplicate work.Meeting Transcripts: Historical Apollo transcripts are missing, causing the "Qualification" dashboard to misrepresent deal status.Narrio Features & Identified ValueCompany Identity: The "xpath global" tab provides a context foundation for Narrio's AI, pulling data from the website and LinkedIn.ICP & Competitors: Auto-generated profiles can be edited for accuracy.Knowledge Base: A section for manually adding URLs, text, or documents (e.g., case studies, G2 reviews) to enrich deal context.Deals List: A high-level view of all deals.Filtering: Allows filtering by "Health" and "Risk" clusters (e.g., "Single Thread," "Stalled") to prioritize work.Deal Dashboard: A detailed view for each deal.Qualification (SPICE): A dashboard summarizing deal context (Situation, Pain, Impact, Critical Event, Economic Buyer).Knowledge: A repository of all communication (emails, transcripts).Email Generation: AI-generated emails based on deal context, with an option to reference specific knowledge items.Activity Reports: Summaries of activity across leads and deals for a selected period.Use Case: Ideal for weekly sales cadences to align the team.Future Feature: Scheduled reports and a chat interface for deeper analysis.Audit Report: Analyzes pipeline health against a revenue target ($250k was entered as a placeholder).Key Insight: The "Stages" view identified a major bottleneck: conversion drops sharply after the "Assessment" stage.Future Feature: An agent to auto-populate deal amounts, improving revenue forecasting.Nestlers Account SetupRequirement: A separate Narrio account is needed for the Nestlers pipeline.Potential Issue: The shared domain between xpath.global and Nestlers may cause a privacy conflict.Resolution: Alexandra will investigate. Doesn't follow up on previous emails regarding new offer but goes on old email trails. Example Xceedance. Looking forward to hearing from you. Happy May Day! 🙂 Best, Dana ------------------------------ *From:* Dana Teodorescu *Sent:* Monday, April 20, 2026 3:20 PM *To:* alice@narrio.app *Cc:* Kevaughn Campbell *Subject:* Intial Feedback Week 1 Hi Alexandra, I'll drop in the feedback as I go along, as I there might be some quick fixes that don't need to wait until our weekly catch up. Please see below, and kindly let me know if I'm doing something wrong in accessing the info. 1. Audit - High potential heath - no next step for LatentView, where I have meeting scheduled. Same as for Brillio. - Quantiphi - no next step/ I had tasks to follow up in Hubspot. Same for Marla and Coupang. 2. Audit Continued - as I filter out, I'd like to click on the deal and have it open. Right now, I need to switch to deals and manually search for it. I applied filter on Needs Intervention - I can't see the number of deals that have that filter applied. I can only see total number of deals in the pipeline. I cannot export the information. 3. Emails taking a while to generate. And nothing to show me it's working on it, in this screen. I need to check notifications to see it's still in progress. Simetimes a hard refresh popus up the email, that seems to have been ready. Thanks a lot. Best, Dana

Meeting PurposeTo explore a Narrio pilot to address xpath.global's sales challenges.Key Takeaways•Pilot Agreed: xpath.global will pilot Narrio for ~1 month to analyze its sales process and test its new "services-first" strategy.•Core Challenge: A long, unpredictable sales cycle driven by conservative HR buyers who are slow to adopt technology and often provide misleading information to avoid being spammed.•Data Gaps: Critical context is siloed in Apollo (meeting recordings) and Outlook (emails), preventing a unified view of each deal in HubSpot.•Narrio's Role: To unify data from HubSpot, Apollo, and Outlook into a knowledge graph, providing AI-driven insights on deal health, stakeholder roles, and next best actions.Topicsxpath.global's Sales Challenges•Unpredictable Sales Cycle: Stage lifetimes vary widely, making forecasting difficult.•Stakeholder Visibility: Sales reps rarely gain access to decision-makers, speaking primarily with user buyers (functional leads).•Misleading Information: Prospects often understate their needs (e.g., "only 5-10 people") to avoid sales pressure.•Internal Hurdles: HR buyers struggle to build internal business cases for technology, facing resistance from conservative departments like compliance and procurement.•Example: A prospect (Arcelor) spent one month preparing a presentation for a VP of technology.•Revenue Tracking: Not a current focus; the primary goal is closing deals, not granular revenue categorization.Current Sales Strategy & Tech Stack•Lead Sources: LinkedIn (via LinkedIn Helper), webinars, events, and newsletters.•CRM: HubSpot is the single source of truth for all leads and deals.•Used in its basic form with custom properties for segmentation; no lead scoring.•Meeting Recording: Apollo provides AI note-taking and video/audio recordings.•Data Silo: Meeting summaries are logged in HubSpot, but the recording links are not, forcing reps to access Apollo separately.•Email: Outlook is used, but emails only sync to HubSpot if the rep manually BCCs the CRM, creating another data gap.•Strategic Pivot: Testing a "services-first" approach, as clients are more receptive to buying services (a "burning need") than technology (a "nice-to-have").Narrio's Proposed Solution•Data Unification: Connects HubSpot, Apollo, and Outlook to build a knowledge graph, providing a single, objective view of the sales process.•Pipeline Audit: Offers leadership-level insights on revenue risk, deal health, and rep performance.•Deal "Zoom-In": Provides deep analysis of individual deals, including:•Progression Timeline: Visualizes the deal's history and identifies stall points.•SPICED Qualification: Automatically analyzes conversations to score Situation, Pain, Impact, Critical Events, and Decision.•Stakeholder Mapping: Identifies all mentioned stakeholders, assigns roles, and tracks sentiment/engagement to facilitate multi-threading.•Next Best Actions: Recommends specific actions to move deals forward.•AI-Powered Tools: Generates context-aware meeting preps and follow-up emails.•CRM Hygiene: Pushes accurate data back into HubSpot to maintain a clean system of record.•Language Support: Understands Romanian and displays insights in English. Performance depends on the quality of the source transcriber (e.g., Apollo, HubSpot's native recorder).Next Steps•Alexandra:•Send a draft NDA to Elena, covering both xpath.global and Nestlers.•Send a Google Meet invite for the onboarding session.•Elena:•Provide company details for the NDA.•All:•Attend the 30-minute onboarding and training session.•When: Tomorrow, 10:00 AM•Who: Alexandra, Elena, Dana, Kev•Goal: Connect HubSpot accounts (xpath.global & Nestlers) and begin the pilot.

activities.subject: RE: Whalebone x Narrio
activities.full_text: Hey, Thank you for the presentation. Some changes are required: 1. Slide 4: 0.15 EUR (not 0.25 EUR). 2. Slide 4: 2 mln subs- starting from 2 mln subs per telco, not average. 3. Slide 4: our sales cycle target is different. On a moment sales cycle is 9-12 months. We want to make it 6-9 months. 4. Slide 4: our time-to-launch target is different. our deployment time can be unpredictably long- we want to standardize it to 3 months. 5. Slide 5: last point- not “for you as SVP”, but “ for Management” 6. I’m missing some slides what are you actually offering (description of your solution) and the solution (PoC/pilot) deployment plan. Thank you! -- Vladislavs Gurmans VP, Global Sales & Business Development vladislavs.gurmans@whalebone.io | +37129335572 | www.whalebone.io Whalebone, s.r.o. Jezuitská 14/13, 602 00 Brno Czech Republic From: Alexandra Botezatu Sent: Friday, April 24, 2026 4:06 PM To: Vladislavs Gurmans Cc: Mircea Serediuc Subject: Re: Whalebone x Narrio Hi Vlad, Really glad we got to meet in person — thank you for the time and for being so open about where Whalebone is headed. I've put together a short proposal based on our conversation. The starting point is the intelligence gap we talked about: knowing how ready a telco is and what's blocking them - proactively and reliably flagging this information from context before the delay has already started. In order to achieve that, Narrio connects to HubSpot, Gmail, and call notes and structures that context into the deal automatically — no behavior change required from the team. The technical session use case is the clearest example of where that matters first, but once the infrastructure is in place there's a lot more Narrio can surface across your pipeline: stalled deals, missing stakeholders, deployment signals, and more. I did use the numbers you shared for the ROI estimates in the deck — the $0.25/user, 0.38% uptake, 2M average subscribers. Given I was taking notes in suboptimal temperatures :) , I'd appreciate a quick confirmation that I got those right. I've kept the proposal focused so it's easy to react to. Happy to walk through it together and figure out what a 12-week pilot would actually look like for your team. Best, Alexandra On Tue, Apr 21, 2026 at 9:59 PM Vladislavs Gurmans > wrote: Great, received. We can be there around 13@00. Give us hint where to find you. activities.full_text: Buna Alex, Meet Eugen! E pus la curent, asteapta semnul tau. Multumesc, Raluca Tătărușanu (Resmeriță) Vice President of Sales – EMEA&APAC Tel.: +40724128020 Email: raluca.tatarusanu@druidai.com Let’s connect on Linkedin [A black and grey logo AI-generated content may be incorrect.] AI that Works to Help People. druidai.com · LinkedIn · YouTube From: Alexandra Botezatu Date: Friday, 13 March 2026 at 15:57 To: Raluca Tatarusanu Subject: Narrio sales deck and summary from our conversation Hi Raluca, It was great speaking with you. Thank you again for the open conversation and for sharing more context on how your team is thinking about CRM structure, reporting, and process right now. As promised, I’m sharing our sales deck here for context. Based on our discussion, a few things stood out to me as especially relevant for your team: First, it is clear you have already put a lot of work into improving CRM discipline and creating more consistency around core metrics and processes in HubSpot. That progress matters, especially given how many teams still struggle to move away from fragmented reporting and manual work. At the same time, it also sounds like there are still natural gaps between what exists in CRM and what is actually happening across deals. For example, fields may exist, but they are not always completed consistently. Important deal context can still remain buried in conversations, notes, or rep memory, especially around topics like competition, stakeholder mapping, and buying dynamics. That is where I believe Narrio could be useful. We help teams improve CRM accuracy, but also go beyond classic hygiene by surfacing the missing context that affects forecasting, pipeline visibility, and deal execution. activities.subject: Narrio sales deck and summary from our conversation
activities.full_text: Hi Raluca, It was great speaking with you. Thank you again for the open conversation and for sharing more context on how your team is thinking about CRM structure, reporting, and process right now. As promised, I’m sharing our sales deck here for context. Based on our discussion, a few things stood out to me as especially relevant for your team: First, it is clear you have already put a lot of work into improving CRM discipline and creating more consistency around core metrics and processes in HubSpot. That progress matters, especially given how many teams still struggle to move away from fragmented reporting and manual work. At the same time, it also sounds like there are still natural gaps between what exists in CRM and what is actually happening across deals. For example, fields may exist, but they are not always completed consistently. Important deal context can still remain buried in conversations, notes, or rep memory, especially around topics like competition, stakeholder mapping, and buying dynamics. That is where I believe Narrio could be useful. We help teams improve CRM accuracy, but also go beyond classic hygiene by surfacing the missing context that affects forecasting, pipeline visibility, and deal execution. I completely agree that the best next step would be a conversation with the RevOps team, since they know the HubSpot setup, roadmap, and process design in much more detail. My hope would be to use that discussion to understand what is already working well, where the current gaps are, and whether there are areas where Narrio could add value faster than building everything internally. Thanks again. I really enjoyed the discussion and I appreciate the intro you offered to Martin and Eugen. Best, Alexandra *Alexandra Botezatu (Alice)* CEO & Co-Founder @ Narrio.app *Higher win rates in complex sales * phone: +4 0748 683 399

activities.subject: Meeting
activities.full_text: Impromptu Google Meet Meeting - March 11VIEW RECORDING - 15 mins (No highlights)Challenges with AI technology adoption @ 2:02The discussion covers the challenges companies are facing with the proliferation of AI technology, as there is a lot of "noise" and confusion around which solutions to invest in. Both companies are struggling to convince their enterprise customers of the value of AI and get them to adopt these new technologies.Changing sales dynamics and budgets @ 4:09The participants note that the sales environment has become much more difficult, with customers being more cautious about spending, especially in Q4. There is less of the typical "use it or lose it" budget mentality, and companies are taking a more conservative approach to technology investments.Raluca's company's CRM and data challenges @ 9:28Raluca's company has faced challenges in getting consistent and accurate data in their CRM system, particularly around metrics like ARR, TCV, and RR. They have had to implement custom fields and processes to try to get better visibility, but still struggle with incomplete and inconsistent data.Opportunity for collaboration @ 12:24The participants agree that it would be valuable to have Alexandra's team do an audit of Raluca's company's CRM setup and data, to identify gaps and opportunities for improvement. They plan to set up a follow-up meeting with Raluca's RevOps team to further discuss potential collaboration.

activities.subject: Narrio x FalkorDB
activities.full_text: Hi all, Great meeting you yesterday. Really enjoyed the conversation and the deep dive into how you're thinking about graph infrastructure. It was especially helpful for us as we shape our own graph layer. As mentioned at the end of the call, here is the link to our technical publication, Hyperplane:https://thehyperplane.substack.com/   We publish long-form technical and product deep dives around AI systems, graph architectures, and applied ML in production. We also have a strong community of developers and technical builders following the publication. As we start documenting more of our graph journey, we would love to feature FalkorDB in a future article if you're open to it. On the Narrio side, I would love for you to experience the platform from the sales perspective once your SOC process timing is clearer. I think your team would immediately recognize some of the pain points we’re solving, especially around deal visibility and context across long sales cycles. Makes sense to reconnect in a couple of weeks as discussed. In the meantime, if any technical questions come up while Rebeca experiments with Falkor, we’ll reach out. activities.subject: Re: Narrio x FalkorDB
activities.full_text: Hi Alex, Dan, Quick check-in - how is the SOC process going on your side? On our end, we have been working closely with a few highly technical product companies, and that is where we have seen the strongest results. In deep tech sales, the usual CRM layer starts to feel restrictive. Long validation cycles, multiple POCs, technical scrutiny, security reviews - the deal reality is much more complex than what the stages show. I was thinking about our conversation and I believe Narrio would fit very well with your org. I would be interested in putting it to the test and setting up a free instance for you. We can connect HubSpot, ingest a limited set of active deals, and review the output together on a working call. No rollout commitment - just a focused test to see if the visibility adds value for your team. Would you be open to scheduling that in the coming days? Meeting with transparent.euTransparent x NarrioDecember 08, 2025  •  30 mins  •  View MeetingUpgrade to Premium to revert to advanced summary templatesIntroductions and status updates @ 0:00The meeting began with brief introductions and status updates from Alexandra, Transparent Solutions, and Adina. They discussed their current workloads and how the day has been going so far.Reviewing the sales opportunity data @ 1:33Alexandra reviewed the sales opportunity data that Transparent Solutions had provided, noting that the notes and context were helpful in understanding the patterns and insights. They discussed the limitations of the data export and the need to supplement it with additional context from emails and other sources.Analyzing the sales opportunities @ 3:13Alexandra presented the analysis of the six sales opportunities, highlighting patterns such as the opportunities being in a "limbo" state for 4-18 months, the involvement of multiple stakeholders, and the value proposition being positioned as non-urgent. She provided specific examples and recommendations for how to reframe the value proposition to create more urgency.Discussing the Jaguar Land Rover opportunity @ 6:24Adina provided an update on the Jaguar Land Rover opportunity, explaining the complex history of communications and the impact of the recent cyber security incident. They discussed how to best re-engage with Jaguar Land Rover given the current circumstances.Exploring opportunities for further analysis @ 25:30Adina and Alexandra discussed the potential to analyze "cold leads" or opportunities where Transparent has had limited engagement, as an alternative to the stalled deals that were the focus of the initial analysis. They agreed to explore this approach further and reconvene in a couple of days to discuss next steps.Recap and next steps @ 27:53The group summarized the key takeaways and agreed on next steps, including Adina following up on the Hilton and Knorr-Bremse opportunities, and Alexandra potentially conducting a similar analysis on a set of "cold lead" opportunities from Transparent's HubSpot pipeline.

activities.full_text: Meeting with Cube DigitalNarrio Onboarding VeridionDecember 09, 2025  •  29 mins  •  View MeetingAction ItemsNo action items detected in this meetingMeeting SummaryMeeting PurposeOnboard Veridion to Narrio and connect their HubSpot account.Key TakeawaysHubSpot Integration Requires Pipeline Filtering: Narrio's "Deal Audit" is unusable without filtering by pipeline ID, as Veridion's HubSpot contains non-sales data (e.g., POCs, recruiting) that would skew the analysis.Sales Battlecard Needs Internal Data: The auto-generated battlecard is inaccurate (e.g., listing incorrect competitors). It requires Veridion to upload internal documents to the Knowledge Base for enrichment.Performance Bottlenecks Identified: HubSpot's API rate limit (1M calls/day) and Narrio's processing speed (100 deals/10s) will cause long initial syncs. A 400 error also occurred during a single deal import.Veridion's Goal: Use Narrio to identify which deals to focus on to close the year strong and which to deprioritize.TopicsHubSpot Integration & Pipeline FilteringProblem: Narrio's "Deal Audit" pulls all deals from Veridion's HubSpot, including non-sales objects like POCs and recruiting pipelines.Impact: This makes the audit results meaningless and unusable for sales analysis.Solution: Narrio must add a feature to filter HubSpot data by pipeline ID during integration.Technical Detail: A 400 error occurred during a single deal import. Vlad (Cube Digital) will investigate the logs.Sales Battlecard AccuracyProblem: The auto-generated battlecard, created from public data (website, LinkedIn), is inaccurate.Specific Inaccuracies:Missing data roles.Incorrect competitors (e.g., CoreSignal).Solution: Veridion must upload internal documents (e.g., case studies, positioning docs) to the Knowledge Base to enrich the battlecard with accurate, "Tier 1" information.Performance & Data SyncHubSpot API Rate Limit: 1 million calls/day.Impact: A sync of ~10,000 deals could consume the entire daily limit, blocking further activity for 24 hours.Narrio Processing Speed: ~100 deals/10 seconds.Impact: Initial syncs will be slow. Users will receive an email notification when the full audit is complete.Veridion's Use CasePrimary Goal: Gain clarity on pipeline health to inform year-end strategy.Key Questions to Answer:Which deals are viable for closing?Which deals should be deprioritized to focus resources?Context: Veridion's HubSpot data is known to be incomplete, making Narrio's insights critical.Next StepsCube Digital:Add pipeline filtering to the HubSpot integration.Investigate and fix the 400 error during deal import.Complete the full "Deal Audit" on Veridion's main sales pipeline.Notify Veridion when the audit is complete.Veridion:Upload internal documents to the Knowledge Base to enrich the sales battlecard.

activities.full_text:
Hi Richard, Teo, Andrei,

Thank you all for your time and insights. Wanted to bring everyone onto the
same page following our conversations.

Across our discussions, a clear picture emerged of what Vox needs and where
Narrio fits.

*What we heard*:
• HubSpot isn't delivering what the sales team or leadership needs: low
adoption, manual workarounds, and reporting that requires significant
effort to produce.
• The AI initiative is about productivity, not replacement - adoption has
to be earned through utility, especially with the sales team
• The Microsoft migration in the next 30–40 days is the natural moment to
reset the data foundation, not work around it.


*What Narrio addresses directly:*• A single commercial data layer that
consolidates HubSpot with the sales reality from emails, calls and
knowledge docs - auto-updated, not dependent on rep input
• Deal intelligence and pipeline visibility that gives leadership the
reporting clarity they need without heavy manual reconciliation and
extraction
• Designed to meet reps where they work — HubSpot, Outlook, Slack — so
adoption isn't a change management project
• Pilot timed to the Microsoft migration means you go live on the right
foundation, not rebuild again in six weeks


*Proposed path forward:*Start with a focused pilot - a defined group, clear
objectives, measurable outcomes. Validate the fit. Then expand to the full
team.

To put a concrete proposal together, one thing I need from your side: *a
rough breakdown of the team: # BDRs, #SPs, ops, and who needs the
leadership reporting view.*

I'm also syncing with Andrei separately next week for a short HubSpot
walkthrough so we can configure the pilot correctly from the start.
-> *Andrei please let me know what works on your end and I will send an
invite* (or you can use my direct calendar link from the signature if
easier).

Attached: compliance brief covering our data and infrastructure model. As
mentioned during our conversations, we have the option to leverage your
choice of LLMs.

Looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Alexandra

>
